2. The complaint case assumed existence out of a petition filed by one Md Gyesuddin, a resident of Chittagong. In his petition the complainant alleged that being desirous to buy a parcel of land, he approached the appellant to obtain latter's opinion of the title of the said property. After examining relevant Khatians, etc., the appellant, gave a clean bill as to the apparent vendor's title and possession over the property in question. He also expressed that the property was free of encumbrances. The appellant, instead of returning the Original Khatian, handed back the photocopies thereof to the complainant. Being stimulated by the said affirmative opinion, the complainant entered into a bainanama in respect to the said land, which venture taxed his pocket by an amount in excess of Taka 5,00,000 in all. At a subsequent stage the complainant got swamped with suspicion about the authenticity of the photocopies of the said documents, which state of his mind propelled him to procure certified copies of the same. Said copies revealed that the subject property was indeed part of government's khas land. He further alleged that the spurious opinion furnished by the opposite party was the outcome of an intrigue espoused by the appellant in connivance with the fake vendor. 

 3. The appellant repelled the complaint tooth and nail and filed a written statement in deminti of the allegations recorded in the complaint instrument. He flatly refuted the allegation that he was supplied with khatians or documents pertaining to the title of the property. His unequivocal reply was that he provided no opinion whatsoever. His part of the story, as narrated in his written statement, was founded on the assertion that the terms of the instruction, under which he was engaged by the complainant, did not extend beyond the drafting of the bainanama and that is all that he did. He also averred that it was obvious from the contents of a complaint petition, which the present complainant filed in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate in Chittagong leading to the commencement of an abortive criminal proceeding against the appellant, that the story of the receipt of "opinion," was a sham one.
